newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Turks seek constitutional recognition.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Turks seek constitutional recognition.

text.p: Bulgaria's ethnic Turkish Movement for Rights and Freedoms on Wednesday called for amendments to the constitution to recognise the presence of a Turkish minority in the Balkan state.
Senior party official Yunal Lyutvi said the time was right for Bulgaria to alter its post-communist constitution, which says there are no minorities in the country.
"The constitution is not adequate to the changes and challenges which Bulgaria faces," Lyutvi told a news conference.

Bulgaria's Turkish speakers total 829,000, or 9.8 per cent of the 8.5 million population, data from the 1992 census show. More than one million people, or 12.7 per cent of the population, are registered as practising Moslems.

In the early 1980s Bulgaria's ethnic Turks were victims of forcible assimilation under former communist dictator Todor Zhivkov. They were urged to adopt Slav names and their religious and human rights were severely curbed.
With the overthrow of totalitarian rule in 1989 their religious and cultural rights were restored and many of those who had left for Turkey have returned.
President Petar Stoyanov is seeking the support of Turkey to remove Bulgaria from a list compiled by the Organisation of the Islamic Conference of countries which do not respect Moslems' rights.

The Movement for Rights and Freedoms, which in coalition with monarchist parties forms the third force in the parliament, would need the support of other parties as changes in the constitution require a two thirds majority.
